title: Growth monitoring from the health record

figures.note: the app with its sample patient loaded: parsed vitals from the record, each marked with how it is used on the chart.

line: single-file SMART on FHIR app reading a child's growth history
question: Can a browser app read a child's growth history straight from a health record and surface faltering a short visit would miss?
calls: growth engine fenced off during the feature build. the percentile tables, interpolation and anomaly rules were the part already checked.
demo cases built around trajectory, velocity and delayed recognition, not population-specific expected growth. a subgroup-specific chart can make a remediable problem look typical.
model API key asked for at run time and held in sessionStorage. the app ships as static files, so anything in the repo ships with it.
self-hosted HAPI added as the custom-data lane, Epic kept as the interoperability lane. only the read source changes; the growth logic does not.
broke: first scopes requested were user-level, which return no patient context. switched to patient-level and printed the granted scopes to debug it.
the sandbox patient came back with no vitals at all, so the chart had nothing to draw. synthetic measurements added as a fallback.
the plain category search for vital signs did not work; the query needs the full terminology system URI, and requests need an explicit FHIR JSON Accept header.
switching between demo patients and plotting the parental target line were both wrong after the feature build.
tried: dropped the Epic OAuth launch in the follow-on build for a HAPI server with a patient dropdown, because the teaching vignettes had to be ones I could author and load myself.
not_shown: percentiles come from a small embedded boys-only table, interpolated, not a validated LMS engine
